articles.title: Salesforce Interview Question: The Customer Paid. Why Isn’t Their Coffee Being Made?
articles.excerpt: One oat latte, a missing payment confirmation, and a system design walkthrough that follows the order all the way to the counter. Imagine Maya ordering an oat latte on her way to work. Her payment goe…
articles.body: One oat latte, a missing payment confirmation, and a system design walkthrough that follows the order all the way to the counter. Imagine Maya ordering an oat latte on her way to work. Her payment goes through, but the café’s tablet never receives the order. She arrives at the counter holding a receipt for a drink nobody has started. Now the retry button looks less like a convenience and more like a very expensive question. Does tapping it recover her coffee, create another order, or charge her again? I love a system design problem that gets interesting before we have even finished ordering breakfast. Everyone understands the customer’s expectation, which makes it much harder to hide a missing guarantee behind an impressive architecture diagram.
articles.author: Emily Woods

articles.title: Replacing Newman and Collection Runners with Spec-Driven CLI Tests
articles.excerpt: Quick answer: A collection runner like Newman is great at replaying a saved set of requests, but it tests the collection, not the contract. When teams want assertions that stay true as the API evolves…
articles.body: Quick answer: A collection runner like Newman is great at replaying a saved set of requests, but it tests the collection, not the contract. When teams want assertions that stay true as the API evolves, a spec-driven CLI that generates requests from the OpenAPI document and validates responses against it is the more durable choice. The migration does not have to be all at once: keep the collection runner for exploratory sequences while moving regression and contract checks to generated, schema-validated requests that fail the moment the API and the spec diverge. Collection runners earn their place early. A developer records a sequence, adds a few assertions, and runs it headless in CI.
articles.author: Jeff

articles.body: We're BrainWave Studio, a tiny independent studio. This month we've been shipping Valaris — a Windows app (plus a web version for phones) that puts hundreds of AI models into one chat. You bring your own OpenRouter account, you see the price of a request before you send it, and your chats stay on your device. No funding, no ad budget. Here's what we learned so far. Why we built it Paying for five AI subscriptions to use each model a few times a month felt wrong. Pay-per-request through one API is usually much cheaper — but the existing tools either hid the price, stored your chats on their servers, or were built for developers only. We wanted something a normal person could install and use.

articles.title: WordPress Images Not Uploading? Fix the HTTP Error and Media Library Problems
articles.excerpt: Originally published on CodingCush. If WordPress will not upload your images and keeps showing a vague “HTTP error”, the cause is usually one of five simple things: the file is too large, the uploads…
articles.body: Originally published on CodingCush . If WordPress will not upload your images and keeps showing a vague “HTTP error”, the cause is usually one of five simple things: the file is too large, the uploads folder does not have the right permissions, a plugin is interfering, your site has run out of PHP memory, or the file name contains characters WordPress dislikes. Start with the smallest checks first — resize the image, rename it with plain letters and numbers, and try again. If that fails, check the permissions on the wp-content/uploads folder, increase the memory limit, and test by temporarily deactivating your plugins. In most cases, one of these fixes solves the problem in under fifteen minutes, without touching any scary code. We know how annoying this feels.
articles.author: Lavkush kumar

articles.title: What moving quote forms get wrong about stairs, elevators and long carries
articles.excerpt: Most moving quote forms ask two questions: how big is your home, and how far are you moving? Those matter, but they miss the details that decide whether moving day takes four hours or eight. Stairs, e…
articles.body: Most moving quote forms ask two questions: how big is your home, and how far are you moving? Those matter, but they miss the details that decide whether moving day takes four hours or eight. Stairs, elevators, long carries and tight doorways are where estimates go wrong, and they are exactly the details a good form should ask about before anyone talks price. Start with stairs. A third-floor walk-up is a different job from a ground-floor flat with the same number of rooms. Every flight adds carries, rest breaks and risk, especially for mattresses, wardrobes and appliances. A form that asks only for bedroom count treats both jobs as identical, and the crew finds out the truth on arrival. Asking "how many flights of stairs, at each end?" is a small question that prevents a large surprise.
articles.author: Daniel Mercer

articles.title: The Quiet Metric: Time to Recover
articles.excerpt: Dashboards love totals. But the metric that quietly decides whether a subscription business keeps its customers is a duration: how long a failed payment stays failed. Every day in that gap is a day th…
articles.body: Dashboards love totals. But the metric that quietly decides whether a subscription business keeps its customers is a duration: how long a failed payment stays failed. Every day in that gap is a day the customer reconsiders, replaces, or simply forgets the service — and a day the next renewal sits at risk. Shortening the gap is mostly unglamorous work. Messages that go out while the failure is still news. Update pages that take ninety seconds instead of nine minutes. Retries placed where the reason says they belong. None of it announces itself; all of it compounds. Swipe Again reports time-to-recover alongside totals for exactly this reason, on every platform down to its Paddle recovery — because a recovery on day two and a recovery on day twenty are not the same save.

articles.title: Bethesda Pays Tribute to Patrick Stewart for His Role in Oblivion, Fans Remember His Role in Games Like Castlevania
articles.excerpt: Bethesda has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart for his role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion after his death.
articles.body: Bethesda has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart for his role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion after his death. Earlier today, it was announced that beloved actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, died at 86 years old . The news came as a shock to many, and social media has been full of tributes to the actor. Many of his longtime collaborators, such as William Shatner, Kevin Feige, and Hugh Jackman all shared kind words about their time working with him. Bethesda also offered up its own tribute by acknowledging the actor's death, calling him an "inspiration to us all." Stewart had a brief role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion as Emperor Uriel Septim VII, who is killed off at the very beginning of the game.

articles.title: Halloween Aboard the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit.…
articles.body: ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano finally gets his wish to fly like Superman aboard the International Space Station during Expedition 37. Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit. Whether individually or as an entire crew, they dress up in sometimes spooky, sometimes scary, but always creative costumes, often designed from materials available aboard the space station.   Take a look at how the station crews have celebrated in years past. For Halloween 2009, the Expedition 21 crew shows off its costumes. Expedition 21 NASA astronaut Nicole Stott shows off her Halloween costume.

articles.title: James Gunn Says It 'Won't Be Too Long' Before DCU Batman Is Cast, Will Be Close in Age to David Corenswet's Superman
articles.excerpt: James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman.
articles.body: James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman. Speaking on a new podcast about James Gunn's Suicide Squad film, the director and DC Studios boss addressed where he's at when it comes to the next Batman. Although Robert Pattinson is playing the current caped crusader, it's expected that he will exist in his own separate universe , away from James Gunn's DCU, while another Batman will join forces with the likes of Superman. He noted that it "won't be too long" before they begin casting the next Batman and debunked rumors that he's already been cast. He noted that he's open to casting anyone for the role, even if they've been in a previous DC movie like The Suicide Squad.
